prose: Atticus is a free, open-source macOS voice assistant built by a 9th grader: hold Control-Option-Space, say what you need, release - it moves windows, finds files, reads your screen and gets tasks done, running on Claude without an API key. Hold-to-talk and press-to-toggle modes are both supported, with instant commands that skip the AI entirely.

The safety design is unusually careful for a side project: Apple's final transcript confirms each voice request before AI tools or learned shortcuts run; reasoning can start during a pause but tools wait for confirmation; toggle recordings hit a review screen after 60 seconds; closing the overlay stops the microphone, workers and voice; and the UI respects Reduce Motion and stays on display.
highlights: Hold-to-talk macOS assistant that moves windows, finds files and reads your screen.
Free and open source; runs on Claude with no API key needed.
Voice requests are confirmed by Apple's final transcript before tools run.
Instant commands bypass the AI for supported built-ins.
Mic and workers stop when the overlay closes; 60s toggle cap with review screen.
